note: Faster bidirectional streaming for small request bodies. When a bidirectional dispatch (dispatch_bidirectional_streaming*, JNI dispatchFullStreaming / dispatchFullStreamingWithHeader) is driven directly by Runtime::block_on and no dispatch timeout is configured, the first two request-body pulls made before the handler returns run inline on the calling thread, so a body that ends within them never starts the spawn_blocking producer, its channel or a producer slot (Rust bench, 64 B echo: ~10.5 us -> ~0.95 us). Pulls made while the response streams, inside a spawned task or under a dispatch timeout still use the producer; backpressure, the streaming request cap (413), abort/panic propagation and the early-response detach are unchanged. The request_close hook now fires whenever the request source was read, inline or through the producer.
